note: The high-water mark for the proof-to-product ratio defined in CONTRIBUTING.md. The rule there has bound since adoption and judged nothing: the budget verb reported a number and always succeeded, so the ratio drifted from 1.62 through 1.5902 to here while gates were added without any of the three outcomes the rule names. This file is the line the verb now enforces. Raising it is a decision that leaves a trace; letting it rise silently is what this replaces.
rationale: Frozen at the ratio measured when the ratchet was installed, not at the rule's 1.0 threshold. 1.0 is unreachable from here without retiring roughly a third of the proof mass, and a line nothing can satisfy is a line nobody reads. This one binds today: any change that raises the ratio must retire equivalent proof mass or record an exception below.

exceptions.rationale: The ratchet refused the change that installed it, three times, and each time the honest move was to record rather than to move the frozen line. Its reasoning lives in scripts/, its criteria live in tests/, and admitting both to the generated-source roster costs a few lines more — all of it proof mass by the rule's own definition. A mechanism that stops proof mass growing cannot be installed without growing some. Recorded because a mechanism whose first act is to quietly raise its own limit teaches exactly the habit it was built to stop. 1.5925 is the measured ratio with the ratchet, its four criteria and their registration in the tree; the frozen line stays at 1.5888 so the cost of this installation stays legible rather than absorbed.

STORY-300 slice 2 generalised the append kernel so a single write is the N=1 case of a batch, and the rest of the suite proves that half by passing unchanged. What it cannot reach is the fold itself — a member seeing its predecessor state, a batch crossing a segment boundary, and refusal leaving the chain untouched — so those criteria are new proof mass with no product counterpart to offset them. Paid deliberately: the fold is now the code path every one of the thirty-two chain-write call sites takes, and shipping it on the strength of tests that only exercise N=1 would be the untested-guard shape this platform has paid for before. First time the ratchet fired on a change other than its own installation.

The acceptance-lane roster was written on 2026-08-19 after the audit found it had never existed anywhere while forty-four records had landed done against it. A roster nothing checks rots the same way the absent one did, so platform-doctor gained a leg that holds it to nine complete, uniquely identified groups — proven non-tautological by removing one group and observing the red. The leg is proof mass with no product counterpart, and it is worth paying because the alternative is a criterion whose members are remembered rather than written, which is the thing the criterion exists to replace. Updated to 1.5972 when the leg gained its three red legs in the doctor suite — an absent roster, a roster that lost a group, and an entry missing a field — which are the criteria that make it non-tautological.

Wave 2.2 gave the platform identity file a revision history the only way available without moving it: a tracked copy inside the newly created platform documents repository, plus a doctor leg holding the two to each other. Two copies of a governing document is normally the defect rather than the fix, and it is admissible only because exactly one of them is checked against the other on every run — so the leg and its two red cases are not optional decoration, they are the entire justification for the arrangement. Proof mass with no product counterpart, paid deliberately.

The Story refusal now names the remedy — the full block roster in order, which purpose anchors exist and that they match as literal tokens, both accepted acceptance shapes, and the vocabulary the two token checks scan for. Its criteria are proof mass with no product counterpart, and they are the thing that keeps the message from going quiet again: two audited sessions were measured reading the validator source to learn a contract it already held, nine days apart, and refusals ran 242 against 132 successful writes that week. Paid deliberately.

AC-1 stated that its own absence blocks the release and nothing checked it — the audit went looking for the consumer and found none, while the receipt sat twenty-nine days and nineteen host minor versions behind through more than thirty releases. The release gate now checks presence and a thirty-day window, proven red by backdating the receipt before it was trusted green. Proof mass in scripts/ with no product counterpart, paid because a stated release consequence with no consumer is worse than no statement at all.

The host-role evidence block was anchored on line numbers, so every edit above a match reddened a file whose meaning had not changed — INC-153 was refreshed three times in one day for exactly that, and the audited week counted twenty-seven such refusals across fifty-four blocks. It now records the matched line content, trimmed, deduplicated and canonically ordered. Both directions were proven before landing: altering one matched line still turns it red, and inserting a line above every match no longer does. Small proof mass, paid to retire a recurring one.

GitHub was publishing this repository's French translation as its code of conduct, because that document is resolved by matching the family and taking the first name in sort order, and .fr precedes .md. Moving the four mirrors under docs/i18n/ leaves exactly one root file in the family, and following them cost push-gate a three-line branch on a new mirrorDirectory field. The three lines are the whole overage. They are worth the budget because the alternative was to compress the branch to one line to fit under it, which is writing worse code to satisfy a metric -- the exact move this exception list exists to make unnecessary.

Five criteria for the narrowest useful version of a fail-closed exemption. The knowledge store had to equal the chain head exactly, on reads as well as writes, so one governed write took all six partitions' retrieval surfaces offline until a hand-run rebase -- which is the whole of the audited week's 38 context injections against 0 knowledge citations. Admitting a trailing read is cheap to write and easy to get wrong in four directions at once, so four of the five criteria are about where the exemption must NOT reach: validate, writes, the disclosure that keeps a stale answer from passing for a current one, and the byte-identical aligned response that means no existing caller has to change. A one-line widening of the guard would satisfy the feature and fail four of them.

The dispatch readiness gate measured presence, which a single-character string satisfies, while claiming to enforce the rule that a ticket must be granular enough for an economy model to execute without inventing. Five criteria: the two citation checks themselves, the file:line form that would otherwise report every conventionally-written pointer as missing, and two that exist only to stop the check overclaiming -- an unparseable command must be counted rather than passed, and a brief with no declared root must say its citations went unchecked. The last two are the whole reason this is worth budget: without them a weaker answer wears the stronger one's clothes, which is the defect class this gate was extended to close, reproduced inside the fix.

Four lines of comment, and they are the only reason the budget moved. OD-31 bought five criteria for the citation check; this buys the correction of the argument those criteria were shipped under. The original comment predicted that an executor which cannot find its citation invents rather than stops, and an adversarial run against the economy model the same day refuted it: both stale-brief runs disclosed, recovered, and corrected the command. The measured cost -- five times the tool calls, twice the wall clock, same answer -- replaces the asserted one in place. A comment that states a refuted behavioural claim is worse than no comment, because the next reader inherits it as evidence.

Eight lines of comment on a one-line precondition fix. The criterion waited on the lock directory rather than the owner record and so raced a lock that was not yet established, failing about half of full-suite runs. The comment costs the budget because the thing worth preserving is not the fix but what the fix declined to do: a contender arriving mid-establishment really does get METADATA_INVALID, that really is defensible fail-closed behaviour, and no criterion covers it. Without those lines the next reader sees a green suite and no trace of an untested path, which is how the shortcut this fix rejected gets taken later by someone with less context.

Two changes to the same budget line. Four criteria for searching the knowledge snippet -- the found case, the three existing fields staying matched, the body staying unsearched, and case folding on the new field -- of which the last two exist only to stop the widening from swallowing the metadata-first discipline it sits next to. And a sealed-owner precondition whose comment costs more than its one line of code, because what it preserves is the boundary the previous attempt mislocated: owner.json is published twice, the second rename replaces the inode, and a read spanning it is refused on identity rather than content. Without that written down the next reader repeats the same wrong fix, which is not hypothetical -- it is what happened here, and the retraction of its three-run proof is in the same commit.

The largest single step this line has taken, and the cheapest to justify. It buys a Markdown link gate that this repository never had -- a published code of conduct spent a day telling readers the authoritative text was at a path that did not exist, through twenty-three P1 gates, sixty-one guard mutations and eighteen doctor legs, and its first run found three further broken citations nobody had noticed. It buys three criteria over the CLI, the only transport a governed session has, whose five hand-written argument lists and five hand-written option objects had nothing asserting the flag survived the trip. And it buys the repair of two criteria written the same day that could not fail -- one passing a flag into an argument nothing reads, one folding case against an already-lowercase fixture. A criterion that cannot fail is worse than no criterion, because it is counted; retiring proof mass to stay under the line would have meant keeping some of that.

One doctor leg and four criteria for a comparison the platform had never made. Two existing checks were green all day while both hosts ran yesterday's skill payload: one proves the deployed copies match the local trust root, the other proves a version string agrees, and a trust root stale together with its copies is invisible to both -- especially since the payload moves without the version string moving. Three of the leg's four answers can collapse into one another, which is where the criteria go: uncomparable must not read as compared-and-equal, and a missing trust root must not read as uncomparable, or a host with no helper at all reports the same green as a correctly aligned one.

Four criteria for separating the chain's lifetime event bound from the protocol's per-document shape bound, and three for the headroom leg that watches the new one. The criterion earning most of this is the second: that raising the chain bound did not loosen the document bound. The change was one edit away from raising the shared constant, which would have quietly permitted eleven-thousand-element canonical arrays and eleven-thousand-key objects to buy chain headroom -- six input bounds loosened, none of them measured, to fix one lifetime bound that had been. Nothing else in the suite would have noticed; that criterion is the only thing that does.

Six criteria for a gate that shipped with none, which is how it carried a host dependency into five consecutive red CI runs while every local run was green. The one that earns this outright puts a real file OUTSIDE the repository and asserts the link to it is still refused -- that is the CI condition asserted rather than hoped for, and nothing else in the suite can see it, because on this machine the sibling checkout makes the broken form resolve. Retiring proof mass to stay under the line would mean keeping a gate whose verdict depends on what else is on the disk, which the host-independence convention forbids outright.

The acceptance-verdict leg now binds each green result to the inspected engine commit and refuses an unbound or different-tree result. This pays for the three red-leg tests that prove a verdict from another commit is stale, a verdict on the current commit passes, and a missing commit is refused, plus the unreadable-HEAD deferral that keeps synthetic fixtures from inheriting a false failure. The old roster-mtime bound had measured negative ages on every live entry and was host-dependent because mtime is not tracked by git; retiring these tests would leave the platform able to report green for a run from a different tree, the exact failure STORY-304 exists to close.

The container batch adds the executable red legs for a scoped acceptance exception, canonical platform-docs migration, whitelist-root admission, and the runtime observation sink move. The extra proof mass is the evidence that these changes do not turn a real failure green or reintroduce a second container authority; it is paid explicitly so the P1 ratchet remains visible rather than being weakened or bypassed.
